# test_camel_to_snake.py
import pytest

from your_module import camel_to_snake   # adapt import to where the function lives


# ---------- Happy-path cases --------------------------------------------------

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "original, expected",
    [
        ("camelCaseString", "camel_case_string"),   # regular camelCase
        ("CamelCaseString", "camel_case_string"),   # PascalCase
        ("aSimpleTest",     "a_simple_test"),       # single leading lower-case
        ("AWord",           "a_word"),              # two-part PascalCase
    ],
)
def test_happy_path(original, expected):
    assert camel_to_snake(original) == expected


# ---------- Edge cases --------------------------------------------------------

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "original, expected",
    [
        ("", ""),                 # empty string
        ("a", "a"),               # single lowercase char
        ("A", "a"),               # single uppercase char
        ("lowercase", "lowercase"),  # already snake-like
        ("HTTP", "http"),         # all uppercase word (acronym)
        ("HTTPRequest", "httprequest"),  # consecutive upper-case block
        ("Version2Update", "version2update"),  # contains digits, no split
        ("àLaMode", "àlamode"),   # non-ASCII first letter – no split
    ],
)
def test_edge_cases(original, expected):
    assert camel_to_snake(original) == expected


# ---------- Error cases -------------------------------------------------------

@pytest.mark.parametrize("bad_value", [None, 123, 12.3, object()])
def test_non_string_input_raises(bad_value):
    """
    Anything that is not a (str | bytes | bytearray) should make re.sub
    raise a TypeError saying “expected string or bytes-like object”.
    The function does not catch that, so we surface it here.
    """
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        camel_to_snake(bad_value)
